- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods; apply a 1–3% upward bias if sentiment > 0.75 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to reflect reversion to prior mean.
